findings.title: Any-to-any permit rule
findings.description: This rule permits unrestricted traffic from any source to any destination.
findings.recommendation: Restrict the source, destination, protocol, and service to only what is required.

findings.title: Static NAT has matching permit ACL
findings.description: Static NAT translation 203.0.113.10 has a matching permit rule 64 that includes the translated address in its destination.
findings.recommendation: Verify that the permit rule is intentionally exposing the NAT resource and restrict source, destination, protocol, and ports to the minimum required access.

findings.title: Potentially exposed SSH service
findings.description: The rule permits SSH traffic on port 22.
findings.recommendation: Restrict SSH access to trusted management networks and avoid unnecessary Internet exposure.

findings.title: Potentially exposed RDP service
findings.description: The rule permits RDP traffic on port 3389.
findings.recommendation: Restrict RDP access to trusted networks and prefer VPN or another controlled remote-access method.

findings.title: Unreachable deny rule
findings.description: Rule 76 is completely covered by earlier permit rule 64.
findings.recommendation: Review the rule order. If the deny is intended to block traffic, move it before the broader permit rule.

findings.title: Potentially exposed static NAT
findings.description: Internal resource object:PUBLIC_WEB is statically translated to 203.0.113.10.
findings.recommendation: Verify that the static NAT is required and ensure associated access-control policy restricts access appropriately.

findings.title: Permit rule is shadowed by an earlier permit
findings.description: Rule 78 is completely covered by earlier permit rule 72.
findings.recommendation: Review the later rule and remove it if it is redundant.
